messages:
sam-support: Hey team — customer hitting intermittent 500s from our hosted API around 2026-03-15 16:10 UTC. Their screenshot has no obvious request id. Can someone paste the minimal repro ask (what to grab from UI/SDK/har/curl) so support can send a single copy-paste to non-dev product folks?

maria-eng: TL;DR: ask for 3 things: 1) the x-redwood-reqref (or request header) / trace id, 2) a HAR or curl that hits the failing endpoint, 3) any SDK logs around the timestamp. Also include exact timestamp (UTC) and the endpoint path.

sam-support: perfect — can you give exact phrasing we can copy to the customer? they prefer step-by-step that a PM can follow.

maria-eng: sure, send this: 

"Please send: (1) the Request Ref/Trace ID shown in your network logs or SDK (header name: x-redwood-reqref or X-Request-Ref), (2) a HAR file or a curl that reproduces the failing request, and (3) any SDK logs exported around the failure time. If you can’t share auth tokens, just include the request headers (except Authorization). Also tell us the UTC timestamp of the failure and which region your request went to."

alex-ux: Add a tiny how-to for the web console: "Open DevTools -> Network, reproduce the error, right-click the failing request -> Copy -> Copy as cURL (bash) or Save all as HAR". Then ask them to open the request details and copy the header value for x-redwood-reqref (or any header that looks like request/trace id).

josh-eng: For SDKs: "JS browser console: look for `reqRef` or `requestId` lines, or enable debug logs `REDWOOD_DEBUG=1` and reproduce. Mobile: iOS crash/sysdiagnose or Android logcat — grep for 'reqref' or 'request_ref'. Example Android command: `adb logcat -d | grep -i reqref`"

maria-eng: Add this safe curl example to demonstrate what we mean (tell customer to replace redacted fields):

```bash
curl -v 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate' \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -H 'x-redwood-reqref: <if-present>' \n  -d '{"input":"test"}'
```

maria-eng: If they can’t share Authorization, ask them to still paste the request headers (screenshot of headers is fine) and send the exact request start time (UTC with seconds) so we can find server-side traces.

sam-support: good — mention proxy/edge stripping too (we keep hitting that).

josh-eng: Right — add: "If you go through a corporate proxy or CDN, the header might be stripped or renamed (e.g., req-ref -> x-req-ref). If you don’t see x-redwood-reqref, share any header that looks like a UUID/hex near the request; we can correlate on timestamp + path."

alex-ux: For HARs: "Save the HAR, then upload the file to the support case. HAR includes headers and request body — please remove any PII before uploading."

engbot: Note: when you open a support ticket with a HAR/curl/reqref, include `customer_region`, `approx_timestamp_utc`, and `sample_path`. Eng team will search traces using those three fields.

sam-support: Also remind customers about debug token from Console: Console -> Request logs -> open request -> Generate debug bundle (redact tokens if needed). That bundle contains server traces and is the fastest path for escalation.

maria-eng: final template for support copy/paste:

"Hi — to help us reproduce & trace this quickly please share: 
1) The request trace id (x-redwood-reqref or equivalent) from your network logs or SDK (or a screenshot of the request headers). 
2) A HAR file or a `curl` (Copy as cURL) that hits the failing endpoint. Please replace your auth token with `<REDACTED>` if needed. 
3) SDK logs around the UTC time: <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS UTC> (please include timezone if local). 
4) If using the Console, generate a debug bundle from the request details and attach it. 

If you’re unable to share tokens, tell us the exact UTC timestamp (with seconds) and the request path so we can look up traces. Please remove any PII before sending. Thanks!"

sam-support: copy/pasting that now. Thanks all :raised_hands:

josh-eng: quick pro-tip for support engineers: if the customer gives you only a timestamp and path, run a time-bounded trace search first, then use any partial header values to correlate — saves time vs. asking for full debug bundle every time.

sam-support: noted — closing this thread once the customer reply arrives. :white_check_mark:
